adherence.reason: The piece is a historical-fiction narrative grounded in the California Gold Rush era.
Elias Thorne is explicitly depicted working as a prospector and repeatedly panning river sediment for gold.
The action takes place on the American River near Sacramento, clearly locating it along a California river.
The 1852 setting remains within the California Gold Rush begun in 1849, which the narration explicitly references as the start of Elias's three-year tenure.
Elias has held the same marked claim for three years while the narration states neighboring claims change hands a dozen times.
The text explicitly reveals that Elias has known the claim was worthless since April 1850 and has bought Sacramento gold dust to fabricate yields.
All present action unfolds continuously during one dawn, with earlier events supplied only as backstory.
Surveyor Vane arrives on behalf of a mining syndicate specifically to inspect Elias's claim.
The narrative action is consistently rendered in present tense; past forms occur only in dialogue and necessary references to antecedent events.
At the close, Elias gives Vane the emptied pan, turns his back on the river, and definitively leaves the claim and his old life behind.
